title: Identify the major PC components
description: Learn what each main part of a desktop computer does and how to recognise it inside the case.
objectives: Name the major internal components of a desktop computer.
Explain the job of each component in one sentence.
Tell volatile memory (RAM) apart from storage.
Recognise each component inside an open desktop case.
tools: Phillips screwdriver (to open the side panel)

safety.text: Unplug the computer and ground yourself before opening the case. See "Electrical safety and ESD precautions".
Heatsinks and some chips can stay hot for several minutes after the computer is turned off.

steps.title: Motherboard
steps.body:
The **motherboard** is the large main circuit board that every other part connects to. It holds the CPU socket, RAM slots, expansion slots (PCIe), storage connectors (SATA and M.2) and the firmware chip (**BIOS/UEFI**) that starts the computer.

Common desktop sizes are **ATX** (305 × 244 mm), **Micro-ATX** and **Mini-ITX**. The size decides which cases it fits.

steps.title: CPU (processor)
steps.body:
The **central processing unit (CPU)** carries out the instructions of programs. It sits in the motherboard's **socket**, usually hidden under a cooler with a fan or heatsink.

A CPU only fits a socket made for it, so the CPU and motherboard must be compatible (for example, Intel LGA1700 or AMD AM5).

steps.title: CPU cooler
steps.body:
The **cooler** removes heat from the CPU. Most are a metal heatsink with a fan; some are liquid coolers with a pump and radiator.

**Thermal paste** between the CPU and cooler fills microscopic gaps so heat moves across efficiently. A CPU must never run without its cooler.

steps.title: RAM (memory)
steps.body:
**Random-access memory (RAM)** holds the programs and data the computer is using right now. It is fast but **volatile**: everything in it is lost when the power goes off.

Desktop RAM comes as long modules called **DIMMs** that click into slots next to the CPU. Laptops use shorter **SO-DIMMs**. DDR4 and DDR5 modules are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Storage
steps.body:
**Storage** keeps files, programs and Windows even when the power is off (it is **non-volatile**).

- **HDD (hard disk drive):** spinning magnetic platters; large and cheap but slower. Connects with a SATA cable.
- **SATA SSD:** flash memory in a 2.5-inch case; much faster than an HDD.
- **M.2 SSD:** a small card that screws directly onto the motherboard. NVMe M.2 drives are the fastest common storage.

steps.title: Graphics card (GPU)
steps.body:
The **graphics processing unit (GPU)** creates the image sent to the monitor. Many CPUs have **integrated graphics** built in. A **dedicated graphics card** is a separate card in the long **PCIe x16** slot, with its own memory and cooling, for games and graphics work.

If a dedicated card is installed, plug the monitor into the card, not into the motherboard's video ports.

steps.title: Power supply unit (PSU)
steps.body:
The **PSU** converts 220 V AC from the wall into the low DC voltages the parts need (mainly **+12 V**, **+5 V** and **+3.3 V**). It powers the motherboard through the **24-pin ATX** connector and the CPU through the **4+4-pin EPS** connector. It also has cables for graphics cards and drives.

Its rating in watts must be enough for all the components.

steps.title: Case and cooling fans
steps.body:
The **case** holds and protects everything and directs airflow. **Case fans** usually pull cool air in at the front and push warm air out at the back and top.

The front panel's power button, USB ports and audio jacks connect to the motherboard with small front-panel cables.

steps.title: Find them inside a real computer
steps.body:
With the computer unplugged and yourself grounded, open the side panel and point to each part in turn: motherboard, CPU cooler (the CPU is underneath), RAM, storage, graphics card if there is one, PSU and fans.

Do not remove anything in this lesson; just identify. If the layout looks different from the examples, check the motherboard manual: layouts vary between models.

expectedResults: You can name every major component and point to it inside a desktop case.
You can explain the difference between RAM and storage.

commonMistakes.why: RAM (memory) is temporary working space; storage keeps data permanently. Mixing them up causes confusion when diagnosing problems or ordering parts.
commonMistakes.fix: Say "RAM" or "memory" for DIMMs, and "storage" or "drive" for HDDs and SSDs.

commonMistakes.mistake: Plugging the monitor into the motherboard when a graphics card is installed.
commonMistakes.why: Most motherboards disable their own video output when a dedicated card is present, so the screen stays black.
commonMistakes.fix: Connect the monitor to the graphics card's ports.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming every motherboard looks the same.
commonMistakes.why: Slot positions, connector names and features differ between manufacturers and models.
commonMistakes.fix: Always check the motherboard manual for its layout.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which component loses its contents when the computer is turned off?
What does the PSU do?
knowledgeChecks.answer: It converts 220 V AC mains power into the low DC voltages (12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V) the components use.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where is the CPU usually found?
knowledgeChecks.answer: In the socket on the motherboard, under the CPU cooler.
